generation_frontiers.warning: Frontier progression is not a clean single-variable causal A/B: v3 starts warm and adds instinctive coverage; v3 controller also compares an ideal-parallel latency index across different coverage modes.

accepted_44x47.interpretation: Instinctive coverage repaired the v2.4 asymmetric failure in latency terms, but did so by spending much more total clone compute. The 204.87 score is not a pure intelligence multiplier.

retry_54x57_after_pitstops.interpretation: On fresh same-geometry retry, the system opened substantially less of the field and spent less total clone compute after learning. Predictive rank itself was not monotonically better, so this is evidence for coverage compression, not a universal prediction improvement.

hard_boss_250x250.interpretation: The large score is an ideal-parallel coverage latency result, not a 21.68x intelligence gain. Total clone compute is worse than STATIC while ideal parallel latency is much lower. Old 250:250 experience did not yet make pure prediction strong.

new_diagnostics.name: COVERAGE_LATENCY_REFERENCE_INFLATION
new_diagnostics.finding: Cold/hybrid parallel coverage can create a very high latency score and thereby inflate the next-stage recovery reference even while total compute is high.
new_diagnostics.consequence: The v3 frontier 44:47 is valid under the implemented controller but should not be interpreted as a mode-invariant capability frontier.
new_diagnostics.next_controlled_fix: Keep v3 frozen; next controller should track latency_index and total_compute_index separately and apply recovery to a mode-normalized or Pareto/balanced metric rather than raw parallel-latency score alone.
